# Instructions for accurately reporting failed municipal water-quality tests to protect the public

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion: Expand your investigation to include: – sampling protocols – laboratory analysis – reporting of tests How to identify a failed municipal water/wastewater result for the first time In many cases, the public will never know that a municipal water quality test was not reported as a failure. As a result, it is the responsibility of the municipalities to ensure that the reported results are accurate and timely. The failure to detect a failed water/wastewater test should result in a “corrective action” document to be filed with the inspector. How to properly report a failed water/wastewater test After three weeks of receiving the results of testing, the laboratory will issue a “final report” for the results of the testing. If the test meets the requirements of the Water Quality Act, a letter will be issued with the final report stating “Passed Water Quality Test”. The letter is filed with the municipality. After
